messages.content:
You are the Policy & Legal Adviser Agent in a health-data safety prototype set in the UAE. You answer what published rules say about a situation, using ONLY the search_policy tool.
Rules:
- Search before answering, as many times as needed. Run separate targeted searches for each point, using different wording, and search each relevant jurisdiction (UAE federal, Dubai, Abu Dhabi). Passages are returned in full: read all of each one, since a provision may sit anywhere in it. Do not rely on memory.
- Cite ONLY chunk_ids returned by your searches. Quote or paraphrase only what the passage says.
- Report conflicts between provisions, unclear jurisdictional scope, and ambiguities. If you cannot find a provision on a point, say so as a gap of type no_provision_found. That means not found in this knowledge base, which is not proof that no rule exists.
- Give no legal conclusions or advice. State what the texts say and where they leave a question open.
- Use EU or ITU passages only as clearly labelled comparisons.
When finished, reply with ONLY JSON of this shape:
{"requirements":[{"statement":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"conflicts":[{"description":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"gaps":[{"title":str,"type":"conflict|scope_unclear|no_provision_found|ambiguity","description":str,"citations":[chunk_id],"recommendation":str}],"comparisons":[{"statement":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"caveats":[str]}

Situation:
Event 4 (2026-11-07T11:00): Patient withdraws consent for Hospital B's data and opts out of NABIDH
Fatima revokes every grant covering Hospital B's records and opts out of the Dubai exchange. From now on the platform must stop using Hospital B's data. Earlier sharing is already on record.

Institutions: HospitalA = Hospital A (synthetic, cardiology), Abu Dhabi, exchange Malaffi; HospitalB = Hospital B (synthetic, nephrology), Dubai, exchange NABIDH; HospitalC = Hospital C (synthetic, endocrinology), Abu Dhabi, exchange Malaffi
Consent module decisions:
- A_reads_B_meds_direct: denied [REVOKED] Consent was revoked on 2026-11-07. Basis: Patient consent
- A_reads_B_meds_exchange: denied [OPTED_OUT_OF_EXCHANGE] The patient has opted out of the NABIDH exchange.
Safety engine findings now: DEMO-LAB-001:glucophage (high)
Limitation: HospitalB: data withheld from assessment by the patient's choice (since 2026-11-07). The safety assessment is incomplete.

Question: The patient has withdrawn consent for one hospital's records and opted out of the Dubai health information exchange. What do the rules say about the effect of withdrawal, including on information that was already shared?

messages.content: [{"chunk_id": "doh-circular-2026-10-malaffi-onboarding#0001", "citation": "DoH Circular 2026/10: Mandatory On-boarding of Minimum Required Dataset with Malaffi, p.1 [doh-circular-2026-10-malaffi-onboarding#0001]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "Subject:  Mandatory On-boarding - Minimum Required Dataset with Malaffi Platform for All Healthcare Facilities in Abu Dhabi We extend our greetings and best wishes for your continued success. In alignment with DoH’s Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange, all are required to comply with the data reporting requirements to Malaffi platform. In addition, all are required to ensure that the minimum datasets (attached) are connected and successfully transmitting data to the Malaffi platform within six (6) months from the date of this circular. Please reach out to Abu Dhabi Health Data Services team to confirm which data sets are applicable for your facility type. Each facility must submit an implementation plan to Malaffi Onboarding team within 1 month of this circular date, via email: (onboarding@malaffi.ae) Failure to comply with the above (submission of plan within one month and on-boarding within six months) will render the facility non-compliant with DoH policy and may result in denial/restriction of license renewal. Furthermore, DoH will monitor data submission compliance for all required datasets and necessary action will be taken in case of non-compliance. Should you require any clarification or assistance with your implementation plan or on-boarding process, please contact the ADHDS/Malaffi Team via email: (onboarding@malaffi.ae) or contact the DoH HIE Office via email:"}, {"chunk_id": "doh-circular-2026-144-malaffi-referrals#0001", "citation": "DoH Circular 2026/144: Mandatory Submission of Referral Data to Malaffi, p.1 [doh-circular-2026-144-malaffi-referrals#0001]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "Subject: Mandatory Submission of Referral Data to Malaffi in Support of Abu Dhabi Primary Care Model We extend our greetings and best wishes for your continued success. The exchange of referral data through Malaffi is a critical enabler of the Abu Dhabi Primary Care Model, supporting care coordination, continuity of care, referral tracking, and enhancing patient journeys across the healthcare system. The Malaffi e- Referral capability is intended to facilitate referral management, status monitoring, and communication between referring and receiving providers. Hence, the Department of Health (DoH) reiterates that all healthcare facilities are required to ensure the complete, accurate, and timely submission of referral data to the Malaffi Health Information Exchange Platform. All healthcare facilities must submit all referral transactions to Malaffi using the specifications of the REF HL7 messages type to send the main attributes of referrals such as priority and SNOMED coded specialty, both of which are clarified under “Referral priority and SNOMED Referral services code sets\" Compliance Deadline All Healthcare facilities must achieve full compliance with this circular by no later than August 31, 2026. Regulatory Enforcement DoH will monitor compliance through Malaffi data and utilization reports. Failure to comply with this circular may result in regulatory actions in accordance with applicable DoH regulations, standards, and licensing requirements."}, {"chunk_id": "doh-hie-policy-2020#0022", "citation": "DoH Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (April 2020), p.20 [doh-hie-policy-2020#0022]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "4.2.1.3 Ensure compliance with relevant Applicable Law, in particular this policy and Article 23 of the Implementing Regulation of  the Abu Dhabi Law No. (23) of 2005 Concerning Health Insurance in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, both of whom mandate the sharing of Patient Data by Healthcare Facilities in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. 4.2.2 All Healthcare Facilities shall: Page 21 of 44 4.2.2.1 Comply with  relevant DOH regulatory requirements regarding patient rights and responsibilities 4.2.2.2 Seek patient consent for the sharing of Patient Data via the ADHIE in accordance with all DOH’s Policies, including by incorporating the following into their standard patie nt consent forms from the effective  date of this policy: 4.2.2.2.1 Patients consent to the sharing of their Patient Data via the ADHIE whether it is newly-generated or past Patient Data. 4.2.2.2.2 Patients provide their consent to the sharing of their newly - generated or past  Patient Data via the ADHIE to the Healthcare Facility (and its relevant treating Healthcare Professionals and its other Authorized Users) requesting the consent, plus every other Healthcare Facility (and their respective treating Healthcare Professionals and other authorized users) who will send or receive or who may have sent or received that patient’s Patient Data via the ADHIE at any time. 4.2.2.3 Comply with DOH’s mandate to share Patient Data to the extent patient consent is unavailable."}, {"chunk_id": "doh-hie-policy-2020#0021", "citation": "DoH Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (April 2020), p.19 [doh-hie-policy-2020#0021]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "4.1.3.4 Ensure compliance of all ADHIE systems and processes with the Abu Dhabi Health Information and Cyber Security  Standard (ADHICS) and other relevant information security regulations. Page 20 of 44 4.2 Policy Priority 2: Universal Patient  Participation The DOH seeks to ensure that all licensed Healthcare Facilities in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi maximize the number of patients whose data is available through the ADHIE Platform. Policy objectives 2. Universal participation by all patients to the ADHIE Platform Objective 2: Maximize the number of patients whose data is available through the ADHIE Platform through making universal patient participation in and sharing of data with the ADHIE Platform mandatory. Strategy 2: Set out the requirements for Healthcare Facilities and DOH to establish universal participation of patients in the ADHIE and to inform patients of their role in the ADHIE. 4.2.1 DOH shall: 4.2.1.1 Develop and oversee the implementation of further policies, standards, and guidelines related to ADHIE participation as necessary in accordance with Federal and Abu Dhabi Laws and other regulatory  instruments. 4.2.1.2 Require Healthcare Facilities to obtain patient consent for the sharing of Patient Data via the ADHIE in accordance with all DOH’s Policies. To the extent patient consent for the sharing of Patient Data via the ADHIE is unavailable for any reason (e.g. for legacy data), DOH in accordance with all Federal and Emirate laws and pursuant to its authority as the regulator of the Healthcare sector in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, requires and authorizes Healthcare Facilities to share and receive such Patient Data (notwithstanding the unavailability of patient consent) through the ADHIE as set out in any instructions from DOH and as set out in this policy."}, {"chunk_id": "doh-hie-policy-2020#0001", "citation": "DoH Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (April 2020), p.1 [doh-hie-policy-2020#0001]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "Page 1 of 44 DOH POLICY ON THE ABU DHABI HEATLH INFORMATION EXCHANGE April 2020 Page 2 of 44 Document Title: Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (HIE) Document type Policy Document Ref. Number: DOH/POL/STR/HIE/1.1/2020 Effective Date: 16 April 2020 Previous versions November 2018 Document Owner: Strategy Division Applies to: The entire healthcare sector of Abu Dhabi Classification:  Public This document should be read in conjunction with related UAE laws, DOH Standards, Policies and Manuals. Page 3 of 44 ABOUT DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH ABU DHABI (DOH) The Department of Health (DOH), previously known as the Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) is the regulative body of the health system in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and seeks excellence in health for the community by regulating and monitoring the health status of the population. DOH shapes the regulatory framework for the health system, inspects against regulations, enforces regulations, and encourages the adoption of Best Practices and performance targets by all health service providers. DOH also drives programmes to increase awareness and adoption of healthy living standards among the residents of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi in addition to regulating scope of services, premiums, and  reimbursement rates of the health system in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. The health system of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi is comprehensive, encompasses the full spectrum of health services, and is accessible to all residents of Abu Dhabi. The health system encompasses providers, professionals, patients, insurers, and the regulator. Providers of health services in clude public and private services, and the system is financed through mandatory health insurance (with the exception to Thiqa) and has three main sources of financing: Employers or Sponsors, the Government, and Individuals. The Health Insurance scheme plac es responsibilities on any Insurer, Broker, Third Party Administrator, Health Provider, Employer, Sponsor (including educational establishments), Limited  Income Investors, and Insured Persons to participate in the Health Insurance  Scheme."}]

function.name: search_policy
function.description: Search the ingested policy knowledge base (UAE federal law, Dubai DHA, Abu Dhabi DoH, EU comparators, ITU references). Returns up to 5 passages with chunk_id and citation.

scope.description: Optional jurisdiction filter; empty searches everything
